title: Northern Railway Station
teaser: The first train was held up because the stationmaster didn't come out to meet it. Drozdov was found behind the locked ticket office, and the money for two tickets to the border was missing from the till. Nobody left town overnight, so whoever took the money is still at the station.

habits.label: Smells of smoke
clues: The locked ticket office smells of locomotive smoke, though the windows onto the platform are sealed for the winter. The culprit's clothes smell of smoke.
The back of the clerk's chair has coal soot on it and a sharp whiff of engine smoke. The culprit's clothes smell of locomotive smoke.

habits.label: Greatcoat without epaulettes
habits.habit: Wears an old greatcoat with the epaulettes removed
clues: A tuft of grey greatcoat cloth hangs on a nail by the ticket office door. The culprit wears a greatcoat.
The buffet attendant remembers a figure at the ticket office after five in a greatcoat with marks where the epaulettes had been unpicked. The culprit wears a greatcoat without epaulettes.

habits.label: Scar on the neck
habits.habit: A jagged shrapnel scar on the neck
clues: The porter saw a turned-up collar at the ticket window and a jagged scar beneath it. The culprit has a scar on their neck.
A note on Drozdov's desk: "The one with the scar on his neck was asking about the night train again." The culprit has a scar on their neck.

habits.label: Medal for Courage
clues: A medal bar with a grey moiré ribbon and blue stripes along the edges was found under the ticket counter. The culprit wears the Medal for Courage.
The duty officer heard metal clink against the glass at the ticket window and made out a medal on a grey ribbon. The culprit wears the Medal for Courage.

habits.label: Rye rusks
clues: There are crumbs of a rye rusk on the ticket office floor, and Drozdov only ever ate in the buffet. The culprit nibbles rusks.
A rye rusk has turned up among the money in the till drawer. The culprit carries rusks in their pocket.

habits.label: Patched felt boots
habits.habit: Wears felt boots with leather-patched heels
clues: There are wet prints of felt boots with leather-patched heels on the ticket office floor. The culprit wears patched felt boots.
A length of waxed thread with felt stuck to it lies on the ticket office doorstep. The culprit wears patched felt boots.

habits.label: Down scarf
clues: Grey goat down is caught on the ticket office latch. The culprit wears a down scarf.
There are grey wisps of down on Drozdov's coat, and his own scarf is wool. The culprit wears a grey down scarf.

habits.label: Harmonica
clues: Towards morning the porter heard a harmonica on the platform, and the tune broke off right by the ticket office. The culprit plays the harmonica.
Under a bench in the booking hall there's a cracked harmonica cover with a German maker's mark. The culprit plays the harmonica.

habits.label: Understands German
clues: "Zwei Karten" is written on the blotter in the ticket office. The culprit knows German.
A German newspaper from the luggage van has been read, with pencil notes in the margins. The culprit understands German.

habits.label: Indelible pencil
habits.habit: Lips stained by an indelible pencil
clues: The figures on a form in the ticket office were written with an indelible pencil that kept being licked. The culprit's lips have indelible pencil stains.
The handle of the cash drawer has purple streaks from a wet indelible pencil. The culprit's lips are stained purple.

habits.label: Hard of hearing
habits.habit: Hard of hearing after shell shock
clues: The duty officer called out twice to the person at the ticket office, but their head didn't even turn. The culprit has been hard of hearing since a shell shock.
There's a sheet on Drozdov's desk with "Speak louder" written on it in large letters, in someone else's hand. The culprit is hard of hearing.

habits.label: Missing little finger
habits.habit: No little finger on the right hand
clues: The dusty glass of the ticket window has a palm print with four fingers. The culprit is missing their little finger.
The bag of small change has prints of four fingers, with no little finger among them. The culprit is missing their little finger.

habits.label: Reads cards
clues: A spread of cards is laid out on the table in the ticket office: a long journey and a government house. The culprit tells fortunes with cards.
There's an ace of spades from someone's greasy fortune-telling deck in Drozdov's pocket. The culprit tells fortunes with cards.

habits.label: Smells of kerosene
clues: The ticket office door handle smells of kerosene. The culprit's hands smell of kerosene.
The cash ledger is spotted with greasy kerosene stains. The culprit's hands smell of kerosene.

habits.label: Grey streak
habits.habit: A grey streak over the forehead
clues: There's a short grey hair on Drozdov's collar, and he's jet-black. The culprit has a grey streak.
The clerk at the next window saw a reflection in the glass: a young face with a grey streak over the forehead. The culprit has a grey streak over their forehead.

habits.label: Stutter
clues: The duty officer heard an argument behind the ticket office door, and one voice stuttered badly. The culprit stutters.
After five someone rang the signal office and, stuttering, asked for Drozdov. The culprit stutters when nervous.

cash: Exactly the price of two tickets to the border is missing from the till, and the rest lies in bundles. The culprit had access to money.
The cash book balances to the kopeck, though there's less money in the drawer. The culprit had access to money.
safe: The fireproof cabinet in the ticket office was opened without force, and there isn't a scratch on the lock. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The safe combination was changed on Monday, yet the safe was opened on the first try. The culprit knows the safe combination.
sched: The ticket office stands empty for ten minutes between the shift change and the first train, and Drozdov was caught there alone. The culprit knows the schedule.
The militiaman patrols the platform at exactly six, and the ticket office door was opened at 06:05. The culprit knows the schedule.
keys: The ticket office is locked from the outside, and there are no signs of a break-in. The culprit had keys.
The left-luggage office was opened during the night and locked again, the lock unscratched. The culprit had keys.
strong: Drozdov's body was carried from the booking hall behind the ticket counter. The culprit is physically strong.
A heavy trunk from the left-luggage office was pushed against the ticket office door to keep it shut. The culprit is physically strong.
quiet: The duty officer sat on the other side of the ticket office wall and heard no footsteps and no creak of the door. The culprit moves silently.
The booking hall floor echoes, yet the passengers asleep on the benches didn't wake. The culprit moves silently.
tech: The ticket office telephone is dead; its wire was neatly taken off the terminal. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The lights in the booking hall went out for ten minutes: a fuse was pulled from the board. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
tools: The ticket window was taken off its hinges and put back, the screws tightened. The culprit is handy with tools.
The bars on the back window of the ticket office were levered out with a crowbar and straightened as if nothing had happened. The culprit is handy with tools.
perfume: The cramped ticket office smells of heavy Red Moscow perfume. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
The handkerchief by the body smells of a thick, sweet perfume. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
cane: There are round dents from a cane in the dusty floor by the ticket office. The culprit walks with a cane.
The buffet attendant heard a cane tapping on the hall tiles five minutes before the noise in the ticket office. The culprit walks with a cane.
passages: A hatch for mail sacks leads from the ticket office to the luggage room, and its bolt has been drawn back. The culprit knows the service passages.
The footprints lead from the ticket office under the platform, to a passage only railwaymen know about. The culprit knows the service passages.
medic: The doctor found no wounds on Drozdov, but the glass of tea on his desk has a bitter residue. The culprit knows about poisons.
The injection went straight into a vein, and the mark on his arm is barely visible. The culprit knows about poisons.
late: The telegraph operator saw a light in the ticket office at three in the morning. The culprit doesn't sleep at night.
Someone drew boiling water from the urn in the buffet after three, when the whole station is asleep. The culprit is a night owl.
driver: There's a fresh tyre track on the station square, and the engine of the lorry is still warm. The culprit can drive.
The key to the official car isn't on its own nail, and there's less petrol in the tank. The culprit can drive.
french: There's a note in Drozdov's pocket: "À la frontière, deux places". The culprit knows French.
A draft telegram in French about two seats to the border lies in the signal office. The culprit knows French.
glasses: A cracked lens from a pair of glasses lies under the ticket counter. The culprit wears glasses.
The ledger in the ticket office has two round marks from glasses laid lenses down. The culprit wears glasses.
